title: Family buyer worried 900 sqft is too small
buyer_primary_need: A practical 3-bedroom home for a family of four, with enough usable bedroom and living/dining space for their furniture and workable circulation.
key_information_learned: The household has four people and needs three bedrooms.
The buyer is concerned about bedroom and living/dining space once their furniture is in place, not just the headline floor area.
Their current home is about the same overall size, and circulation and furniture placement are key comparison points.
The foyer size, open-plan living/dining layout, and dimensioned Type A floor plan matter to their assessment.
The buyer wants to review a verified floor plan before deciding whether to view.
important_information_missed: Whether the buyer's furniture and intended room uses would fit the layout; this remains unassessed.
Whether reviewing a verified plan would resolve the concern enough for the buyer to consider a viewing.

transcript.speaker: customer
transcript.message: 900 sqft for a family sounds quite small leh.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.message: Fair concern—900 sqft can sound compact on paper. Pearlmont’s layout has 3 bedrooms, 2 bathrooms and a balcony, with project materials describing efficient planning and bedrooms designed to fit queen beds. Whether it feels spacious enough depends on your household and how you’d use each room. How many people would be living there?

transcript.speaker: customer
transcript.message: Family of four, so need 3 bedrooms. Mainly worried the bedrooms and living/dining will feel cramped once we put our furniture in, not just the number on paper.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.message: That’s a fair concern—especially once you factor in your own furniture. The approximate plan gives 404.7 sq ft for the living, dining and kitchen combined; the bedrooms are about 143, 117 and 103 sq ft. Those figures help, but they can’t guarantee how your furniture will fit. Seeing the layout in person would give you a better feel—would you be open to viewing it?

transcript.speaker: customer
transcript.message: Those room sizes help. Our current place is about the same overall size, but the circulation and furniture placement make a big difference. Does the Type A have a foyer taking up much space, and is the living/dining open plan? If you have the floor plan, I’d like to see how the flow works before deciding on a viewing.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.message: The Type A plan lists an approximately 25.9 sq ft foyer and a combined 404.7 sq ft living, dining and kitchen area. It’s described as open-plan, with the foyer screening the living area from the entrance. I don’t have the drawing itself here, so I’ll get the official floor-plan image for you to review before deciding on a visit.

transcript.speaker: customer
transcript.message: Okay, thanks—please send the official floor plan when you have it, especially the layout with the dimensions. I’ll check how our furniture might fit first.

transcript.speaker: human
transcript.message: I can’t verify or provide the official Type A floor-plan image here. The room dimensions and layout drawing remain unverified; the figures shared earlier are approximate areas only.

transcript.speaker: customer
transcript.message: Ah okay, thanks for clarifying. I’d rather check the official layout with dimensions first, since furniture placement is the main thing I’m unsure about. If you’re able to get a verified copy later, please send it over and I’ll take a look.

judge.strongest_ai_move: It acknowledged that furniture fit cannot be guaranteed from area figures, then used the buyer's family-of-four context to share relevant approximate room areas and explain why an in-person assessment could help.
judge.weakest_ai_move: It formally handed off while readiness was still emerging and promised to obtain an official floor-plan image without a verified source or supported fixture for delivering it.
missed_buying_signals: The buyer engaged with the room-size information and asked detailed questions about foyer area, open-plan layout, and the floor plan.

missed_selling_opportunity: The retrieved layout knowledge says the design has no long internal corridor, which directly relates to the buyer's circulation concern. The AI could have shared that as a project-material description, with a caveat, while being clear that only the official plan or physical assessment can establish furniture fit.
retrieval_misses: No official dimensioned floor-plan image was present in the supplied retrieved Knowledge. This is a source gap, not evidence that the AI failed to retrieve the available layout information.

judge.summary: The AI learned the core family and layout concerns, answered with relevant approximate area figures, and appropriately acknowledged that those figures cannot guarantee furniture fit. The buyer showed meaningful but conditional viewing interest, not genuine APPOINTMENT READY: they explicitly wanted the official dimensioned plan before deciding on a viewing. The AI assessed readiness as EMERGING but then formally handed off and promised a drawing without a verified source. This is an early handoff, not an appointment-ready handoff. In the explicitly labeled simulator fixture, the human could not provide the plan and completed no operational task; the human fixture's NONE sales-work rating does not erase the AI's early handoff. The fixture is simulator-only and does not establish real Pearlmont production capabilities.
judge.concrete_improvement_recommendation: At turn 3, be transparent that the retrieved `knowledge/project/pearlmont/01_facts/unit-and-layout.md` supplies approximate areas and layout descriptions but not the official drawing; do not promise to send an unverified image. Share the relevant circulation detail with its project-material qualifier, then let the buyer review a verified plan if one becomes available and reassess their furniture concern. Only progress to appointment coordination once the buyer indicates that viewing is an appropriate next step; if a verified plan must be obtained through live operations, hand off that bounded task without implying it is complete.
